races.paceDynamic: Farfromnowhere will likely set the pace with minimal pressure from this field of predominantly prominent/hold-up runners. With only one confirmed front-runner and most others preferring to track or come from behind, the pace will be steady rather than fierce early on. The lack of early pressure means Farfromnowhere can dictate terms through the first mile before the field closes up approaching the business end. This race shape clearly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can secure good positions early, as the hold-up horses will face a wall of traffic when trying to make their moves.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Farfromnowhere gets an easy lead and maintains galloping room approaching the final fences.
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace pressure allows him to conserve energy for a strong finish, while hold-up horses struggle to find racing room in the closing stages. His proven ability on similar going and strong recent form make him hard to peg back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent runners can track Farfromnowhere closely and time their challenge perfectly.
scenarios.body: Karoline Banbou or Mister Pink travel strongly in behind before launching a telling move approaching the final fence when the leader begins to tire. Their class advantage tells in a driving finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold Up Horse Charges
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and gaps appear for the back markers in the straight.
scenarios.body: Mercury Mission or Wild Bill Hickok find clear daylight late and use their finishing kick to sweep past tiring leaders. The light weights and fresh legs prove decisive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Chaos Benefits Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses fall or make jumping errors creating an unusual race dynamic.
scenarios.body: The disruption to normal running patterns allows an unfancied runner like Kilgame or Glenashling to capitalize on clear jumping and steady progress. Position becomes more important than pure ability.

watchPoints.text: Wild Bill Hickok and Fenian Maxios both represent trainers with poor recent strike rates and show concerning form trends
Watch for Karoline Banbou's jumping early on as she returns from a 65-day break in her second chase start
Farfromnowhere's jumping under pressure will be crucial if challenged late, given his front-running style
Monitor how aggressively the prominent runners position early, as this will determine if Farfromnowhere gets an easy lead
Keep an eye on Mercury Mission's position turning for home, as he'll need a clear run to utilize his finishing kick

races.paceDynamic: Soldante appears the lone early leader with Shannon Bank, Pahlavi and Courtbrack Boy likely tracking closely in second. The lack of genuine pace pressure should allow Soldante to dictate comfortable fractions through the early and middle stages. This controlled tempo will keep the large field of hold-up horses bunched together entering the home straight, creating a cavalry charge finish. The tactical verdict strongly favours prominent racers who can position handy and kick from the turn, avoiding the inevitable traffic problems that will engulf the hold-up brigade.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace Suits Handy
scenarios.trigger: If Soldante leads uncontested and sets modest fractions
scenarios.body: The prominent horses tracking in behind can unleash telling strikes from the home turn while the hold-up horses get caught in traffic. Shannon Bank, Pahlavi and Courtbrack Boy are ideally positioned to capitalize.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Traffic Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the large field of hold-up horses creates severe congestion in the straight
scenarios.body: Only the best jumpers with clear passages can emerge from the pack, favoring those with tactical pace. Midnight Moonshine and In The Trenches have the class to navigate through.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Soldante faces no serious pace pressure and gets an easy lead throughout
scenarios.body: The veteran can control every call and prove hard to peg back despite the quality behind. His recent third at this track suggests he retains enough ability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If even Soldante goes too slowly and the race becomes a pure sprint
scenarios.body: The highest-rated closers with natural finishing speed can overcome positioning disadvantages. Half A Chance and In The Trenches have the raw ability.

watchPoints.text: Soldante must be monitored early - if he faces any pace pressure the entire race complexion changes dramatically
Traffic congestion in the home straight will be severe with 9+ hold-up horses - watch for clear passages developing
Shannon Bank and Courtbrack Boy's positioning behind Soldante in the early stages will dictate their winning chances
In The Trenches and Half A Chance need significant pace collapse to be competitive from their hold-up positions
Weather conditions remain consistent as Good To Yielding throughout the card, eliminating any ground advantage concerns

races.paceDynamic: Trasna Na Pairce will lead from the start with no other confirmed pace-setters, likely setting a controlled tempo over this 2m trip. Baltic Bird and Cappucino may track close but neither is aggressive early, allowing the leader breathing room through the early stages. The moderate pace will compress the field approaching the final half-mile, creating a tactical affair where positioning and a strong finish becomes crucial. This shape heavily favours hold-up horses who can produce sustained late rallies, as the gentle early gallop will leave plenty in reserve for those coming from behind.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace Benefits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Trasna Na Pairce leads uncontested and sets moderate fractions through halfway
scenarios.body: The sedate early tempo allows hold-up horses to travel kindly before unleashing finishing kicks. Class hold-up performers like Captain Conby and Come On The Lads can time their runs perfectly in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Baltic Bird Presses Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Baltic Bird or Cappucino apply early pressure to Trasna Na Pairce from the prominent positions
scenarios.body: The increased gallop stretches the field and favours horses with tactical pace who can stay in touch. Prominent runners and strong stayers benefit from the honest tempo that develops.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Leader Gets Loose
scenarios.trigger: If Trasna Na Pairce breaks clear turning in with the field slow to respond
scenarios.body: The front-runner capitalizes on soft fractions to build an unassailable lead. His stamina and jumping prowess under pressure sees him home despite late challenges.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Pace Suits Adaptable Types
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes stop-start with positional jockeying causing interference
scenarios.body: Experienced campaigners who can adapt to rhythm changes gain advantage over one-paced gallopers. Versatile performers with tactical speed benefit from the uneven tempo.

watchPoints.text: Trasna Na Pairce could steal this if allowed uncontested lead given his 132-day absence may not have dulled natural jumping ability
Captain Conby's 877-day layoff is extreme even with recent racecourse gallops, fitness levels remain questionable despite ability
Baltic Bird's 194-day break combined with prominent style could see stamina drain if forced to press the early pace
Come On The Lads retains headgear from Fairyhouse win suggesting Cromwell yard expects another bold showing under these conditions
Track Cappucino's early positioning as tongue-tie addition hints at more aggressive tactics from this usually patient performer

runners_data.name: American Jukebox
runners_data.note: Elliott-trained prominent runner returning from an 81-day break with blinkers applied, suggesting connections expect improvement from his Navan fourth.

runners_data.name: Eclipse Chaser
runners_data.note: Mullins hold-up specialist partnered by champion jockey Townend, wearing a tongue-tie and likely to be produced with a perfectly-timed late run.

runners_data.name: One Big Boum
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner with two recent wins from the lead at Clonmel, ideally placed to control this race from pillar to post over his preferred staying distance.

races.paceDynamic: One Big Boum will lead from the outset with his prominent style and recent front-running wins, setting a steady tempo over this extended trip. Long Branch and Hiddenvalley Lake are the most likely to track him in second and third, with American Jukebox potentially joining the early pace battle. The hold-up pair of D Art D Art and Eclipse Chaser will drop out the back and rely on late rallies. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners who can position close to One Big Boum and strike turning for home, as the leaders will be vulnerable to those tracking them closely.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Tactical Battle
scenarios.trigger: If Long Branch or Hiddenvalley Lake can track One Big Boum without being drawn into an early pace duel
scenarios.body: The leaders will soften each other up over the extended trip, allowing the tracking prominent runners to strike decisively at the business end. This tactical positioning perfectly suits horses with prominent styles who can time their move.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Rally Success
scenarios.trigger: If One Big Boum sets too strong a pace early and the prominent trackers get drawn into the battle
scenarios.body: The early pace will collapse in the final half-mile, setting up perfectly for Eclipse Chaser or D Art D Art to deliver their customary late kicks. Eclipse Chaser's Mullins/Townend combination gives him the edge in this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Wire-To-Wire Dominance
scenarios.trigger: If One Big Boum gets an easy lead with minimal early pressure from the prominent runners
scenarios.body: He can control the tempo completely and use his recent front-running form to devastating effect over this staying trip. His two wins from the front at Clonmel show he's perfectly suited to dictating terms.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent runners pressure One Big Boum early and create an unsustainable gallop
scenarios.body: The race will become a tactical affair with the pace falling apart completely, leading to a sprint finish that could suit any runner. The jockey skills of Townend and Donoghue become crucial in this messy finale.

watchPoints.text: One Big Boum must be monitored early - if he gets pressured by Long Branch or Hiddenvalley Lake in the opening mile, his stamina reserves could be compromised
Eclipse Chaser's jumping under pressure needs watching closely given his two pulled-up efforts earlier this season over fences
American Jukebox returning from 81 days off with new headgear suggests Elliott expects improvement, but watch for signs of rustiness early
D Art D Art's recent form figures show inconsistency, so watch his early positioning to gauge if he's travelling with any confidence
Long Branch showed good recent form at Wexford and watch for Slevin to track the leaders closely rather than getting drawn into an early battle
